words.definition: Lasting for a very short time.
words.example: Social media stories are ephemeral — gone in a day.
She summarized the salient points of the report.
I appreciated the candor in his feedback.

words.definition: Just coming into existence and beginning to develop.
words.example: The startup is still in its nascent stage.

words.definition: Able to be defended against attack or objection.
words.example: That argument is no longer tenable given the new data.
Smartphones are now ubiquitous in daily life.

words.definition: Dealing with things sensibly and practically.
words.example: She took a pragmatic approach and shipped the simplest version first.
He made a cogent argument for cutting the feature.

words.definition: To make something less severe or harmful.
words.example: Caching helps mitigate the load on the server.

words.definition: Stated or appearing to be true, but not necessarily so.
words.example: The ostensible reason for the delay was weather.

facts.title: What merge sort does
facts.body: Merge sort splits a list in half repeatedly until each piece is one item, then merges the pieces back in order. It reliably runs in O(n log n) time regardless of the input.

facts.title: Why the sky is blue
facts.body: Sunlight hits air molecules and scatters. Shorter blue wavelengths scatter far more than red, so blue light reaches your eyes from all over the sky.

facts.title: The Rosetta Stone
facts.body: Discovered in 1799, it carried the same decree in three scripts. Because one was Greek, scholars could finally decode Egyptian hieroglyphs.

facts.title: What a hash function is
facts.body: A hash function turns any input into a fixed-size string of characters. The same input always yields the same output, and a tiny change to the input changes it completely.

facts.title: Why we have seasons
facts.body: Earth's axis is tilted about 23.5 degrees. Seasons come from that tilt changing how directly sunlight hits each hemisphere — not from distance to the Sun.

facts.title: What an API is
facts.body: An API is a contract: it defines how one program can ask another for data or actions without knowing how the other works inside. You call it the same way even as the internals change.

facts.title: Why ice floats
facts.body: Water is unusual: it expands as it freezes, so ice is less dense than liquid water. That is why ice floats and lakes freeze from the top down.

facts.title: The printing press
facts.body: Gutenberg's movable-type press, around 1440, made books cheap to copy. Ideas spread far faster, fueling the Reformation and the scientific revolution.

facts.title: What caching is
facts.body: A cache keeps a copy of expensive-to-fetch data close by, so repeat requests are served fast. The tradeoff is freshness: a cached copy can go stale.

facts.title: Why the moon has phases
facts.body: The moon does not make its own light — it reflects the Sun's. As it orbits Earth, we see different fractions of its lit half, from new moon to full.
